mentl/08d4959:
The stamp's debt is paid, and its first move was the enumeration it said
it owed: 29 LFn sites across lower.mn and wasm.mn, with spec_closure_name
measured orthogonal — it mangles monomorphization twins, not nested-fn
qualification. That cleared the way to the construction site.

The divergence is one expression. lower computes fn_name as outer plus
name when outer is non-empty, then built LLet(handle, name,
LMakeClosure(handle, fn_ir, ...)) — the binding taking the source name
while the LFn inside carried the qualified one. Two names for one
function, agreeing only because outer is empty at every site until the
discriminator works. They take the same name now.

Byte-identical and still worth landing. fn_name equals name wherever
outer is empty, which is everywhere today, so the emit could not move and
the march confirms 412781 lines on both sides. What changed is the
invariant the closure emit depends on: its self-capture early-bind is
guarded by captures_self against fn_name, a string compare that answers
false the moment the two names diverge, skipping the bind and leaving the
closure's fn_ptr a zero local. Same vocabulary-first shape as the row
tail slot — put the invariant in place while it costs nothing, so the
behaviour change lands alone.

What remains, so this is not read as the fix: the captures still
reference the fn by its source name, so a self-capture under
qualification is not consistent end to end. That is the next step, and
only after it does the annotation that opened this arc become marchable.

The march at cfbdf8e confirms the structural predictor worked: m3 went

mentl/0819237:
The first move of the ADT/AST/graph unification: carry the handle, read
live, delete the parallel ADT. PExpr was a lossy COPY of expression
structure the AST node already holds (node_to_pexpr re-derived it with a
`_ => PEVar("?")` surrender). Now Predicate's leaves carry the live
operand Node and every consumer reads its Expr live:

- types.mn: PExpr deleted; Predicate = PTrue | PCompare(BinOp, Node, Node)
  | PAnd | POr | PNot | PBoolNode(Node) | PPatternMatch(Pat, Node).
  show_predicate reads operand nodes live (show_pexpr retired).
- parser.mn: expr_to_predicate + node_to_predicate + node_to_pexpr +
  pexprs_of collapse into one node_to_predicate; the lossy PTrue/PEVar
  surrenders dissolve into `_ => PBoolNode(node)` (every form has a home).
- verify.mn: predicate_decide reads operands via node_const; the three
  pexpr_*_decide functions collapse into litval_compare; pexpr_to_smt ->
  node_to_smt.
- infer.mn: the predicate creators carry the node, not node_handle(node).
- gradient_delta.mn: the where-clause reuses show_predicate (three
  re-derivation functions deleted).
- cache.mn: predicate serializers carry the operand's bounded Expr;
  unpack reconstructs a synthetic node (Verify reads the Expr).

Net -128 lines; the Carried-Truth fix is always toward less code. Isolated
from the ev-slot first-light seam. The unsurpassable-tier sequel
(AST-in-graph, NProgram(NodeBody)) makes the operand a resolvable handle
and lands the e-graph.

mentl/08a53ef:
Per SYNTAX.md:117-124, single-line fn body uses no braces:
  fn double(x) = x * 2          # canonical

parse_block_expr now checks final_count == 0 (no stmts) AND span's
start_line == end_line. When both, emits warning via eprint_string with
the SYNTAX.md-prescribed message and span coordinates. Uses direct
eprint_string rather than `perform report` because (1) the report effect
handler's tier2-perform path traps in this context (pre-L1 substrate gap)

The if uses explicit `else { () }` due to a separate seed substrate gap:

and the compiler inserts implicit `else { () }`. Seed traps instead.
Named follow-up #134 (Hβ.lower.if-no-else-implicit-unit-else) tracks
the substrate-honest fix; this commit uses canonical explicit else.

mentl/08976c4:
The self-hosted Lux compiler can now compile AND execute programs
with algebraic effects. This is a landmark achievement — the compiler
understands its own most powerful abstraction.

=== Parser (parser.lux, +181 lines) ===
- HandleExpr(body, arms, state_bindings) AST node
- ResumeExpr(value, state_updates) AST node
- EffectDeclStmt(name, ops) AST node
- parse_handle: handle { body } [with state = init] { op(params) => body }
- parse_resume: resume(value) [with name = expr]
- parse_effect_decl: effect Name { op(params) -> Type }

=== Codegen (codegen.lux, +170 lines) ===
- Effect opcodes: Perform(110), PushHandler(111), PopHandler(112), Resume(113)
- effect_ops map: EffectDeclStmt registers ops for Call → Perform routing
- Handler bodies compiled as separate FnProtos via ctx_child
- Handler tables: (op_name_idx, proto_idx, param_count) entries
- compile_handle_expr: state inits + handler protos + PushHandler + body + PopHandler
- compile_resume_expr: stateless (Resume+0) and stateful (Resume+N+offsets)
- Context extended to 10 elements (added effect_ops, handler_tables)

=== VM Bridge (vm.rs, +90 lines) ===
- load_chunk extended to parse handler tables from self-hosted output
- extract_handler_tables, extract_handler_table: handler entry deserialization
- fn_proto tuples support optional 9th element for handler tables
- chunk tuples support optional 5th element for handler tables

=== Verified ===
- Fail effect: handler intercepts fail(), returns 42 (not body 99)
- Console effect: say() prints via resume() — hello, world, final: 42
- Multi-shot continuation replay: working through self-hosted pipeline
- All golden tests pass

celezdial/0887b7b:
On a phone the chain, listen, and action rows ran off both edges of the
screen on one clipped line instead of wrapping. The details.cel-veil
had no width constraint, so it grew to its widest non-wrapping child.
The action row was display:flex with no wrap, so its seven buttons gave
the veil a min-content width wider than the viewport; that width then
kept the chain and listen rows from ever needing to wrap.

Pin .cel-veil to width:100% max-width:600px like its siblings, and add
flex-wrap:wrap to .cel-listen and .cel-veil-actions. Verified with a
headless render at 415px: chains wrap after glass, listen after Big
System, actions after Link, nothing clipped.

stoop/0844748:
An eleven inch sheet in an 860 pixel column meant scrolling sideways to see
your own back cover, which is a poor way to judge a page. The sheet now
scales to fit and the whole imposition is visible at once.

zoom rather than a transform, because zoom takes part in layout: a scaled
sheet leaves no hole underneath it and the caret still lands where it is
aimed in a contenteditable panel. Print resets it, paper being already the
right size.

The photo tray moves from the press to the photo concern, which is where it
belonged and which keeps both files under the line ceiling. 02-dither becomes
02-photos: intake, dithering, and placing one on a page are one job, because
a photograph in this app exists in order to end up on paper.
